ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $3.00 voucher (RD-2 mileage refund) to the rider and send the driver's account for review under RD-6
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip: the fare record shows base $3.90 + distance $15.14 for 10.74 km + time $4.29 + platform $1.47 = $24.80 [F6], so distance actually drives the fare and the RD-2 RydeTAXI branch governs the remedy, not a comparison between the 8.4 km quote and the meter [RD-2].

One off-route segment is recorded: 12:12–12:16, 2.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km and reaching up to 954 m off the optimal path [F3]. Nothing exempts it. The rider-requested stop route (RD-3) is unavailable: no stop is recorded in the segment and there is no rider message naming any place [F7][RD-3]. Consent under RD-5 also fails: the chat record contains no rider message at all [F7], and the driver's "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a post-trip statement, which under G11 is a claim and not the rider's pre-segment agreement — so with a complete chat record and no rider agreement before 12:12:15, the segment counts [F8][RD-5]. The traffic excuse fails on its own terms: no incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F11], and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) and band 5 (40–49 km/h), never the band 1–2 severe range, with fair weather [F9][F10][F12][RD-4]. The segment is therefore un-exempted under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

Amount, per the trace formula: rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.40968/km; 2.13 km × $1.40968/km = $3.0026 → $3.00 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The residual ~0.18–0.2 km between the trip excess of 2.31 km ($3.26 billed) and the segment's 2.13 km is out-of-segment mileage that RD-2 does not refund, the time component of $4.29 is not a mileage unit, and waiting was $0.00 with no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on line, so no FARE-1 item arises [F4][F5][F6][RD-2][FARE-1].

RD-6's additional action is triggered: this case upholds a route deviation against the driver (refund > 0), and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, i.e. a repeated breach in the window [F14][RD-6]. The profile is used only for that added action, not to establish the deviation, which F1/F3 establish independently [F1][F3]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, the chat record and the driver's statement — the rider's "He never asked" and the driver's meter/GPS explanation contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8]; nothing to escalate [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment, the fare components and the rate are all recorded [F3][F4][F6].

segment_findings.reason: No rider-requested stop is measured in this segment and no rider message names any place, so RD-3 gives no exemption [F7][RD-3]. The only purported justification is the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him, which is a claim and not the rider's own pre-segment consent under RD-5 (G11); the chat record is complete and contains no rider agreement before the 12:12 segment start, so the segment counts [F7][F8][RD-5]. No RD-4 incident exists on the replaced stretch and the recorded speed bands are 4 and 5, well outside band 1–2 [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. The 2.13 km extra is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as to the metered framing — the fare record confirms meter components (base $3.90 + distance $15.14 for 10.74 km + time $4.29) [F6], and RD-2's RydeTAXI branch is applied; this claim is consistent with the ruling.
Accepted: the single segment adds 2.13 km of the +2.3 km trip excess and the ~0.2 km residue is not refunded under RD-2 [F1][F3][RD-2].
Accepted as to consent: no rider message exists and the driver's statement is post-trip, so no RD-5 exemption arises [F7][F8][RD-5].
Accepted as to RD-4: with no incident near the route and only bands 4–5 in fair weather, neither (a) nor (b) exempts the segment [F9][F10][F11][F12][RD-4].
Accepted in amount: 2.13 km × $1.40968/km = $3.00 is the RD-2 figure, with waiting $0.00 and no ERP/toll item [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].
Accepted as a cap direction but not as the refund figure: RD-2 refunds the un-exempted segment's extra_km only, so $3.00 (2.13 km) is granted rather than the whole billed $3.26 excess [F3][F4][RD-2].

Rejected: RD-6's condition is met by this case's upheld deviation plus the profile's 2 upheld route disputes in the 90-day window, so the account flag is a proper additional action; the profile is not used to decide the deviation itself [F14][F1][F3][RD-6].

Accepted: the complaint, chat record and driver statement contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation and weather was fair, so no safety escalation arises [F7][F8][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Accepted: the driver's profile records 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days and this case upholds another deviation, so the RD-6 flag is imposed based on the profile plus the established violation, not the profile alone [F14][F1][F3][RD-6].
